# Owner-authority installation readiness

**Status: NOT EXECUTED.** This plan was generated by the implementation task
and deliberately not run. No host privilege was used, no system service was
installed or started, and nothing under `/etc`, `/var` or `/run` was created or
modified. Do not execute any privileged command below before the independent
audit of this repair has completed.

Regenerate this plan at any time, unprivileged:

```
python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer plan \
    --authorized-launcher <launcher>
python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer plan \
    --authorized-launcher <launcher> --json
```

## 1. Pre-install conflict checks (unprivileged, safe)

```
python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer preinstall-checks
```

Reports, as JSON:

- whether any of the three fixed roots, the installation record or the public
  key already exists (each is a blocking `ALREADY_PRESENT` conflict, including
  the case where the path is a symlink);
- whether a content-attestable system cryptographic executable resolves, with
  its path and SHA-256;
- whether the current process holds the privileged identity.

Install only when `installable` is `true`. If a conflict is reported, an
earlier installation exists: run the uninstall/rollback plan first, and be
aware that it destroys every provisioned authorization.

## 2. Privileged installation

```
sudo python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer install \
    --authorized-launcher <launcher>
```

The installer refuses unless the effective uid is 0. It performs only bounded
operations: create the fixed directories, generate the Ed25519 signing
identity, publish the fixed public installation record, install the broker unit
definition, and set exact ownership and modes. It reads no credential, contacts
no network, starts no service and provisions no authorization.

### Exact objects, ownership and modes

| kind | owner | mode | path |
|---|---|---|---|
| directory | `root:root` | `0755` | `/etc/admissible-owner-authority-v1` |
| file | `root:root` | `0444` | `/etc/admissible-owner-authority-v1/installation-v1.json` |
| file | `root:root` | `0444` | `/etc/admissible-owner-authority-v1/owner-authority-signing-key.v1.pub.pem` |
| directory | `root:root` | `0700` | `/var/lib/admissible-owner-authority-v1` |
| directory | `root:root` | `0700` | `/var/lib/admissible-owner-authority-v1/private` |
| file | `root:root` | `0600` | `/var/lib/admissible-owner-authority-v1/private/owner-authority-signing-key.v1.pem` |
| directory | `root:root` | `0700` | `/var/lib/admissible-owner-authority-v1/authorizations` |
| directory | `root:root` | `0755` | `/run/admissible-owner-authority-v1` |
| socket | `root:<launcher-group>` | `0660` | `/run/admissible-owner-authority-v1/broker.sock` |
| file | `root:root` | `0644` | `/etc/systemd/system/admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service` |

The private signing key must never be readable by the ordinary launcher, the
controller, the backend, the witness store or the Docker broker; it is never
packaged in a wheel or sdist, and never passes through argv, environment or
IPC.

## 3. Broker service

```
sudo systemctl start   admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
sudo systemctl stop    admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
sudo systemctl status  admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
sudo systemctl enable  admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
```

The unit runs `python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.broker_service` as
`root`, with `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome`,
`PrivateTmp`, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute`, `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX`, and
write access limited to the state and runtime roots. The service entry point
accepts no arguments; it attests the fixed installation and binds the fixed
socket.

## 4. Owner authorization provisioning (privileged, once per launch)

Preview the payload first, unprivileged — this shows exactly what would be
authorized and prints the fingerprint the owner must confirm:

```
python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.provisioner summarize \
    --owner-payload <payload.json>
```

Then, as the owner:

```
sudo python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.provisioner provision \
    --owner-payload <payload.json> --phrase-fd 3 3< <(cat)
```

The provisioner refuses a non-root effective uid; uses the fixed installation
and state roots; accepts one exact canonical owner payload; displays a bounded
summary containing the repository HEAD, run identity, mission, model and
reasoning effort, destination authority, effect authority, budgets, and the
zero retries / zero repairs / one launch policy; requires the owner to re-type
the payload fingerprint; reads the phrase only from the dedicated bounded
descriptor; retains only its digest; writes a root-owned immutable
pending-authorization record; and authorizes exactly one launch.

There is no provisioning operation on the runtime broker socket, and no public
library function callable by an ordinary process creates a production
pending-authorization record.

## 5. Post-install verification (unprivileged, provider-free)

```
python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer verify
```

Confirms the installation attests from its fixed root-owned paths and reports
the installation identity, the signing-key fingerprint, the authorized launcher
uid, the broker protocol and the re-attested cryptographic executable. It runs
no model, contacts no provider and reads no credential.

Then, still provider-free, run the capsule suite and the synthetic privilege
witness:

```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_admissible_capsule_*.py
tests/run_capsule_suite_in_namespace.sh tests/test_admissible_capsule_*.py
```

## 6. Uninstall and rollback

```
sudo systemctl stop    admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
sudo systemctl disable admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service
sudo python3 -m admissible.capsule.owner_authority.installer uninstall \
    --confirm-destroys-authorizations
```

Uninstall requires the explicit confirmation flag because it destroys every
provisioned authorization, including any that were consumed. It prints the
exact paths to remove:

- `/etc/admissible-owner-authority-v1`
- `/var/lib/admissible-owner-authority-v1`
- `/run/admissible-owner-authority-v1`
- `/etc/systemd/system/admissible-owner-authority-broker-v1.service`

Removing the state root destroys the signing key. Every receipt ever issued
under that installation becomes unverifiable, which is the intended rollback
semantic: a reinstall produces a new installation identity, and no receipt from
the old one can authorize a launch under the new one.

## Remaining unknowns

These cannot be closed without the real privileged install and a real canary
run, and are deliberately left open:

- the real installation identity, device and inode values, and the real
  signing-key fingerprint;
- whether the intended launcher account and group are the ones an operator will
  actually run under;
- behaviour of the systemd unit on the target host, including whether
  `RuntimeDirectory` and `StateDirectory` interact as expected with the fixed
  paths;
- the real owner phrase, which exists only in the owner's possession and has
  never been present in this repository or in any test;
- end-to-end behaviour against the real pinned Codex canary with a real
  ChatGPT login, which no test here performs.
